_hinweis: Draft for step 5 (club sizes, Objectives page). Sits in the subfolder because the loader only accepts keys for existing rules; move it to texte/ together with the rules. The board writes formally, the manager replies formally; ziele.stand.* are lines on the Objectives page (informal). In all objective texts: {zahl} = agreed target position, {platz} = current league position. siegesserie_presse: {zahl} = consecutive wins. niederlagenserie: {zahl} = consecutive defeats. Placeholders: {verein}, {platz}, {zahl}, {reporter}, {medium}, {vorstand}.

standard: Season objective: position {zahl} or better
The board has deliberated over the season. We consider position {zahl} or better an appropriate objective. Please let me know whether you support it. – {vorstand}
We need a shared objective for this season. Our proposal: position {zahl} at least. If you rate the squad differently, say so now. – {vorstand}
Agreed. Position {zahl} or better is our objective.
That's too little for me. With this squad I want to finish higher.
I think that's setting the bar too high. I propose a more cautious objective.
Then we'll put that on record. The board will measure the season against this objective.
We're glad to hear it. Bear in mind: whoever announces more is also measured against more.
The board will go along with that, if reluctantly. We expect you to achieve this objective safely, then.
Season objective achieved
Position {platz}: the objective for this season is achieved. The board thanks you and the team for your work. – {vorstand}
We wanted position {zahl} at least; it has turned out to be position {platz}. You have kept to what was agreed. The board is satisfied. – {vorstand}
Thank you, I'll pass that on to the squad.
Season objective missed
Position {zahl} or better was agreed; the final position is {platz}. The objective has been missed. The board will review the season with you. – {vorstand}
Position {platz} does not meet our standards. We had agreed on position {zahl}. That will play a part in the assessment of your work. – {vorstand}
Understood. I'll face that conversation.
The board has proposed a season objective. Accept it or change it.
On course: you're in position {platz}. The objective is position {zahl} or better.
Objective in danger: you're in position {platz}. The agreed objective is position {zahl} or better.
{zahl} wins in a row for {verein}
Win number {zahl} in a row for {verein}
{verein} have won {zahl} games in succession. {reporter} ({medium}): “The team doesn't always play beautifully, but right now they know how to win games.”
The run goes on: {verein} make it {zahl} wins in a row. {reporter} ({medium}) asks who is supposed to beat this team at the moment.
Defeat number {zahl} in a row for {verein}
{verein} slide deeper into crisis
{verein} have now lost {zahl} in a row. {reporter} ({medium}): “The team looks unsettled. They need a morale boost fast.”
{zahl} defeats in a row, and it's getting restless at {verein}. {reporter} ({medium}) writes that the next games will decide the mood across the whole club.
{verein} on course for promotion
Position {platz}: {verein} knocking on the door at the top
{verein} are in position {platz} and so in a promotion spot. {reporter} ({medium}): “Officially nobody there wants to talk about promotion. But the table is already talking.”
Position {platz} after strong weeks: {verein} can dream of promotion. {reporter} ({medium}) urges calm, as nothing has been decided yet.
{verein} stuck at the bottom of the table
Position {platz}: it's getting serious for {verein}
{verein} are in position {platz} and so in a relegation spot. {reporter} ({medium}): “Anyone still talking about a snapshot is misjudging the situation.”
Relegation battle: {verein} find themselves in position {platz}. {reporter} ({medium}) sees a team that can do more but shows it too rarely.
The board is worried
I'll be frank: doubts are growing on the board about the way things are going. We still stand behind you. But we soon need signs that things are looking up. – {vorstand}
The mood on the board has darkened of late. Individual members are asking questions I can no longer answer easily. How do you intend to counter this? – {vorstand}
I understand the concern. In the next games you'll see a turnaround, and I stand by that.
The path is right, it just needs time. I ask the board for patience.
I work with what the club puts in front of me. Whoever wants results has to let me work.
We take you at your word. If the turnaround doesn't come, it will be difficult for all of us.
Patience is in short supply on the board. I'll make the case for it, but I can't promise anything.
That tone won't be forgotten on the board. I advise you to deliver results soon.
Tailwind from the board
Some welcome news: the board is satisfied with the progress. Your work is being noticed at the club, and you have our full support. – {vorstand}
At the last meeting your name came up several times, and in a good way. The board believes you and the team are capable of a good deal this season. – {vorstand}
Thank you. The credit belongs to the team; we'll keep working quietly.
Glad to hear it. Then we should talk about reinforcements.
Thanks for the confidence. I think we can set our sights higher than before.
That's what we expect of you. That attitude goes down well on the board.
You're seizing the moment, I understand that. I'll raise it at the next meeting, but don't expect miracles.
Bold. The board likes to hear that and will remind you of it.
